finalText:
Four canvases use the **maude** design system, all in `ui/panels/`: **GitPanel**, **DiffView**, **GitHubIdentity** and **RepoBranchSwitcher**. The only other canvas, `ui/v2/00 Index`, is already on maude-v2.

A dry run of the switch says all four can move: nothing pins them to maude, and both systems pass the same checks. These are the things that would need attention:

**1. Coloured callouts and the danger button would lose their styling.** This is the main issue. maude-v2 has a plain `.callout` but no info, success, warn or error colours, and no danger button style. These canvases use them:
- **GitPanel:** the info callout for the "Get latest" nudge (lines 320 and 322) and the warn callout for "Publish didn't go through" (line 364).
- **GitHubIdentity:** the red Sign out button (line 249) and the edge-states column, which uses all four callout colours (lines 262–294).
- **DiffView:** one info callout (line 187).

Someone has to decide whether to add these styles to maude-v2 or restyle those elements on the canvases.

**2. The canvases still load maude's files and wrapper class directly.** Each canvas imports `system/maude/colors_and_type.css` and `system/maude/preview/_components.css`, and wraps its content in a `maude` class. maude-v2 only styles content inside a `.ds` wrapper, so the wrapper has to change too, or even the plain callout won't pick up v2's look. RepoBranchSwitcher has six of these wrappers; the others have one each. The checker can fix the imports and wrappers automatically.

**3. Old token names need renaming.** All four use `--accent-muted`, `--accent-tint` and `--canvas-bg/dot/grid`, and RepoBranchSwitcher also uses `--presence-agent`. maude-v2 still accepts them as aliases, so nothing breaks right away, but the checker suggests changing them to `--accent-soft`, `--selection` and the `--x-*` names.

**4. The look will change.** maude-v2 has an azure accent and about 240 tokens against maude's 153, so all four will look different after the switch. They're all marked handed-off, so whoever took them over should know.

**5. Smaller things:**
- Each canvas has about 20–35 warnings for hard-coded font sizes, font weights, spacing and inline SVG icons. They're warnings only and don't block the switch.
- GitPanel has one element locked by a person: the "Changes" tab (line 258). The switch shouldn't need to touch it, but if it does, someone has to unlock it first.
- Both systems have an out-of-date `tokens.json`, so it's worth regenerating those before the move.

I didn't change any files or write a switch proposal. Two commands I tried were denied automatically because no one could approve them: a status check and a script to list every token. I got the same information through other checks.
